bug_semantics: libsoup SoupServer HTTPS accept starts g_tls_connection_handshake_async() with tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb and a raw SoupServerConnection* user_data, passing a NULL GCancellable. soup_server_disconnect() walks priv->clients, calls soup_server_connection_disconnect(), and the disconnected handler drops the server's ref; after the initial_msg cycle is broken, that can finalize the connection while the GNUTLS handshake is still pending. When the handshake later completes, the callback calls soup_server_connection_connected(conn) (then soup_server_connection_get_iostream) or soup_server_connection_disconnect(conn) on the freed object, crashing the server (CWE-825 DoS).
flaw_origin: a89a4910bc356736451b77da3c6389fdf49858c6 replaced soup_server_connection_setup_async's GTask-backed handshake (g_task_new(conn, ...) so GTask held a ref on the connection and was the async user_data) with soup_server_connection_accepted, which calls g_tls_connection_handshake_async(..., NULL, tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb, conn) and has the callback immediately use conn. That is the first write of the UAF-prone callback; parent 1c9e8620754b68aa5520561ceb4fa2ce9516de63 still used GTask and did not pass conn as handshake user_data.

evidence: CVE.org/Red Hat CNA CVE-2026-2436 and GHSA-wpfw-5xvc-wq9w (withdrawn_at null) describe SoupServer UAF: soup_server_disconnect() frees connections while a TLS handshake is pending; tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb then uses a dangling SoupServerConnection. Not withdrawn/rejected.

First-party issue https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libsoup/-/issues/501 (YWH-PGM9867-161) quotes tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb calling soup_server_connection_connected(conn) after free, and names MR !495 as the fix.

Debian tracker cites https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libsoup/-/commit/e9b681a5b23f8259a5e29c5351a5284ae5cd1189 as the fix. Ubuntu notes libsoup2.4 is not affected: server-side g_tls_connection_handshake_async lives only in libsoup3 soup-server-connection.c.

git log -S tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb -- libsoup/server/soup-server-connection.c: name first appears in 25e96cad (GTask user_data). git log -L :tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb:libsoup/server/soup-server-connection.c from a89a4910^..e9b681a5: a89a4910 rewrites the callback to take SoupServerConnection *conn and call soup_server_connection_connected(conn); 5fb25e7810498170dd3458c9509035cef945e299 only adds HTTP/2 protocol selection on that already-raw pointer; e9b681a5 is the cancellable check.

BIC a89a4910bc356736451b77da3c6389fdf49858c6 (Carlos Garcia Campos <cgarcia@igalia.com>, 2022-07-19 author / 2022-08-12 committer, single parent 1c9e8620754b68aa5520561ceb4fa2ce9516de63, not a merge/squash): libsoup/server/soup-server-connection.c tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb at lines 406-414 uses conn; soup_server_connection_accepted at 474-477 calls g_tls_connection_handshake_async(..., NULL, tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb, conn). soup_server_connection_accepted is absent at the parent.

Reachability: soup_server_message_new refs the connection (msg->conn = g_object_ref(conn)); a89a4910 already stores that as priv->initial_msg, so a conn<->message cycle delayed finalize. 6308303e29bbd09966e431cde2df55b879b8df92 (2022-12-13) adds g_clear_object(&priv->initial_msg) in disconnect_internal, allowing soup_server_disconnect to actually free the object during a pending handshake. That leak-fix did not write the callback; it is not the BIC.

reasoning: CVE-2026-2436 is a live Red Hat CNA record (GHSA withdrawn_at null) for a SoupServer TLS-handshake use-after-free, not a withdrawn advisory. The hunter-named sink is tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb using SoupServerConnection after soup_server_disconnect has dropped the last ref while g_tls_connection_handshake_async is still outstanding. git log -L shows that callback first took a raw SoupServerConnection* and called soup_server_connection_connected(conn) in a89a4910bc356736451b77da3c6389fdf49858c6, when setup_async/GTask was replaced by soup_server_connection_accepted. The immediate parent still created a GTask on conn (which refs the source object) and passed that task as handshake user_data, so the connection object was not used as an unowned async pointer. a89a4910 is a single-parent, non-merge rewrite of those lines, not a move/squash, and the parent tree lacks soup_server_connection_accepted and the conn-userdata handshake. HTTP/2 commit 5fb25e78 only reads priv on the already-raw pointer. The Dec 2022 leak fix 6308303e made soup_server_disconnect actually finalize the object by breaking the initial_msg cycle, which is why the reporter's free-after-disconnect path is live from 3.3.0 onward, but it did not first write the flawed callback. The master fix is e9b681a5 (cancellable cancelled in finalize, checked in the callback; identical 3.6.6 cherry-pick 31052a23). BIC membership starts at 3.1.2, before those patched tags. AI is judged only from the BIC commit object: human Igalia author/committer and no AI trailers, so NOT_AI.
